subject: Post-demo: embeddings vs hyperscalers — proposed cloud benchmark & next steps
messages:
From: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>
To: Jay Patel <jay.patel@acmeindustries.com>, searchops@acmeindustries.com
Cc: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.ai>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 3 Aug 2026 10:15:00 -0700
Subject: Post-demo: embeddings vs hyperscalers — proposed cloud benchmark & next steps

Jay — thanks again for carving out time this morning. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we have alignment.

What we covered (recap)
- Acme goals: improve document search recall for support KB and decrease retrieval latency for in-app search (target p95 < 120ms).
- Current baseline: BM25 + sparse signals; pilot with third-party vector provider showed recall@5 ~ 0.62 on sample, avg retrieval latency ~180ms (including network).
- Key decision factors for you: recall@5/10, rerank quality (MAP), per-query cost for vectors stored (monthly), and predictable p95 latency at scale.

Redwood differentiators we highlighted
- Unified runtime: same API & observability across hosted, dedicated, and private deployments so you can validate in-hosted then move to dedicated if needed.
- Cost controls: intelligent batching + prefix caching and quantization profiles that reduce per-vector compute by ~30–50% vs naive runs.
- Graceful fallbacks: automatic routing to cheaper variants when latency SLOs are at risk.

Proposed benchmark (what we suggested on call)
- Test matrix (quick):
  * Candidates: Redwood embeddings (rw-embed-1536 / quantized variant) vs AWS Bedrock text-embedding-ada-002-equivalent and GCP Vertex embeddings (512/768 dims).
  * Rerank models: Redwood-rerank-small (optimized on-device) vs native hyperscaler re-rank endpoints.
  * Metrics: recall@5, recall@10, MRR, MAP, retrieval latency (p50/p95), end-to-end rerank latency (p95), and estimated monthly vector storage + query cost ($/M queries).
  * Data: use the 10k sample you approved (attached: acme_poc_sample_10k.jsonl) — documents + canonical query set + relevance labels.
  * Scale: run locally for 1k queries, then 10k, then a 50k pass if results look promising (gives better p95 signal).

Immediate asks from Acme (please confirm)
1) Confirm we can use the attached 10k sample for the test.
2) Confirm target timeframe: can we run initial 1k/10k passes within 10 business days?
3) Any constraints on running against Bedrock/Vertex from your side (credentialing / procurement)?

Next for Redwood (what we'll do)
- Dylan + Ben: assemble benchmark harness, run embeddings + rerank runs with identical candidate sets, capture recall@k and latency distributions.
- Grace: produce a cost comparison (vector storage, per-query compute) normalized to ACME query profile.
- Monica: coordinate logistics and timeline with you.

Attaching the plan and the 10k sample. If that timeline looks okay Jay, we'll kick off tomorrow and share a preliminary results note within 7 business days.

Thanks,
Monica
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
m: +1-415-555-0123

Attachments: acme_poc_sample_10k.jsonl (10k sample), redwood_cloudbench-plan-v1.pdf
From: Jay Patel <jay.patel@acmeindustries.com>

Cc: searchops@acmeindustries.com, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 3 Aug 2026 12:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-demo: embeddings vs hyperscalers — proposed cloud benchmark & next steps

Thanks Monica — appreciate the clear summary. A few quick confirmations:
- Yes, you have permission to use the 10k sample; it's scrubbed and good to go.
- Timeframe works: initial 1k/10k passes within 10 business days is fine. If we see step improvements we can allocate budget to a 50k pass.
- For Bedrock/Vertex runs: procurement will need a short SOW; I can get that started but expect 3–5 business days for approvals. If you need access earlier, let us know and we can provide a limited-key to our test org.

One detail from our side: our product team really cares about retrieval latency under typical SaaS network conditions. When you run local-hosted Redwood vs hyperscaler endpoints please simulate 50–100ms egress to mimic our infra. That will help give realistic p95s.

Also, could you add a simple cost normalization column: cost per 1M queries (assume avg query returns 20 candidates) so we can compare vector storage + compute + API fees?

Thanks — Jay
Sr. Search Engineer | Acme Industries
From: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.ai>
To: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.ai>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 3 Aug 2026 13:30:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-demo: embeddings vs hyperscalers — proposed cloud benchmark & next steps

Looping internal owners and sketching an execution plan based on Jay's confirmations. Key assumptions pulled from call & Jay's reply: simulate 50–100ms egress for hyperscaler endpoints; use 10k sample; initial 1k/10k passes; add cost normalization to $/1M queries.

Execution plan (owners + ETA)
- Harness & runs (Ben) — Deliverables: repeatable benchmark harness (dockerized), run scripts for rw-embed-1536 (quantized) + Bedrock + Vertex, produce raw metrics and lat/throughput traces. ETA: 7 business days for 1k/10k.
- Rerank comparison (Ben + Grace) — Rerank experiments: candidate set size 100, hybrid rerank (sparse+dense baseline), then full dense + rw-rerank. Track recall@5/10, MRR, MAP, and inference latency p95. ETA: parallel with harness, 7 business days.
- Cost model (Grace) — Normalize to $/1M queries assuming avg 20 candidates returned and 50k vector storage. Include storage price (S3/Hyperscaler vector store), inference compute per 1M queries, and API fees. ETA: 5 business days.
- Infra & credentials (Monica) — Work with Jay to get Bedrock/Vertex credentials or use their limited-key. Also request whether they prefer tests to run from our hosted region (us-west) or from a sim-hosted VM that injects egress.
- Exec check-in (Vivek) — quick 20m sync after first run to decide next steps (50k pass or dedicate capacity).

Benchmark details (parameters we will use)
- Embedding dims: Redwood: 1536 (native) vs Bedrock: 1024 equiv vs Vertex: 768. We'll also test a 768-quant variant to compare storage/cost tradeoffs.
- Retrieval + rerank: candidate recall measurement at k=5 and k=10. Target delta for Redwood: +0.05 recall@5 over baseline to consider win.
- Latency goals: aim for end-to-end rerank p95 < 250ms for hosted; target < 120ms for dedicated deployment. For hyperscaler endpoints include 50–100ms egress in simulation.
- Cost targets: provide cost banding; show where quantization + batching reduces per-query compute by ~30% in previous runs.

Data & reproducibility
- We'll version the harness and share results in the Drive link in the thread. All runs will be dockerized and parameterized so we can re-run from Acme if needed.

If no objections, we'll kick off tonight (Ben will start the harness). Monica can confirm credential path with Jay.

— Dylan
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference

Action items (who/what)

- Ben: begin harness setup and run rw-embed-1536 baseline; report 1k results to the thread.
- Grace: prepare cost normalization spreadsheet and include storage assumptions.
- Dylan: coordinate rerank config and ensure egress simulation is enabled for hyperscaler runs.
- Monica: will book the 20m check-in with Vivek the day after we share 1k results.

I'll follow up if anything blocks. Looking forward to getting a clean apples-to-apples comparison for recall and latency.

Best,
Monica
